title: You Can't Have Christ Without His Cross
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: Jesus does not promise us the peace of this world. Knowing him is the greatest joy there is, and it comes by taking up our cross and forsaking all else.
exhortation: We are not promised peace from Jesus. This is a hard saying, and it doesn't promise us good relationships and peace with everyone around us. In fact, it promises the opposite.

It makes me think about how dearly I hold my family peace, my work peace and my community peace. So much of our American culture is engineered to make me love this world and the peace of this world. Not the kind of peace that Jesus brought, but the kind of peace that leads to hell if it's the only thing we care about.
He says very clearly in verse 38 that you are not worthy of Christ without his cross. You can't have one without the other. You don't get to cherry-pick. You can't have Christ without his cross.

There is a wondrous joy in knowing Christ. Following Christ is the best decision I ever made. If you're listening and you are not following Christ, I encourage you: he is the greatest joy you will ever have in this life. But it does come by forsaking all else. You can't have Jesus and serve money. You can't have Jesus and still make sex your god. You can't serve Jesus and make worldly success your all. You can't have Jesus and make a perfect family the thing you care most about. We must take up our cross and follow our Lord and Savior with a whole and complete heart.

So this morning, Lord, that is our prayer. We pray that we would follow hard after you. Help us root out any divided heart in us, so that no matter the circumstances we would be bold for you and for your kingdom. In Jesus' name.
prayer: Lord, remind us that we are at war. We're at war with our own flesh and our own sin. We're at war with a world that hates your name. And remind us how to fight this war: by proclaiming your grace. I pray that we wouldn't look at others and hate them, but seek to display and declare your grace. It was your grace that saved us.

May your gospel go forth. May we not wilt in times of pressure and darkness and persecution and pain. Strengthen us by your mighty hand, so that in our weakness we might be strong in you, declaring your gospel to our last day, that your name might be glorified in all the earth. In Jesus' name, amen.
